# Buyer architecture: the running system

Checked against `main` at `185ad65` on 10 October 2026. This page explains the implemented buyer. [Design](design.md) describes planned work; [learnings](learnings.md) records what practice showed; [system review](system-review.md) lists risks to investigate.

The buyer tries to minimize total cost over the case horizon. Unit price is only one part of that cost: uncovered demand, payment, freight, delivery, quality, tooling, index clauses and sometimes supplier relationship cost also matter. The final action is one accepted term sheet or a walk-away.

## System map

The supplied diagram shows the live negotiation and what happens after it. The runner owns the session and clocks; the negotiator owns decisions for one case. The model can help write a paragraph, while code sets the offer and closing action.

![Simplified buyer system map, from supplier data and negotiation through arena results and human review](assets/system-map.png)

## Example: one supplier quote

This is an **illustrative routine case**, not a recorded session. Suppose we need 1,000 units, the supplier quotes €100 per unit, the buyer's alternative costs €110,000, and the selected non-price terms stay the same as the quote. The supplier has no special signals that change the usual price path.

1. **Arena → Runner.** The arena opens the case with the supplier's email and quote. The runner fetches the quote, starts one `Negotiator` for the case, and watches the supplier's 60 second reply clock.
2. **Data package → Side → Cost engine.** The negotiator reads supplier facts and quote terms. Its `Side` remembers this supplier's quote, profile and planned terms. The cost engine checks the allowed options and must-haves. In this simple example, the routine opening anchor is 82% of the comparable €100 quote, so the first sheet offers **€82 per unit**.
3. **Writer → Arena.** Code puts €82 and the complete term sheet in the email, plus up to three verified claim sentences if the data supports them. The optional model may write a short paragraph; it cannot change the sheet or figures. The runner sends the message to the arena.
4. **Supplier reply → Negotiator.** Suppose the supplier counters at **€95** with the same terms. `Side` records that counter. With no special rule triggered, the policy moves 30% of the €13 gap from our €82 offer toward €95: **€85.90**. The writer sends this next sheet, with at most one new claim.
5. **Close gate → Arena.** Suppose the supplier later makes **€90** its standing final sheet. The buyer does not accept on price alone. If `total_cost` values that complete sheet at €98,000, it meets every must-have, and the alternative is €110,000, the close gate accepts it. If no standing sheet passes those checks, it walks away. With several suppliers, it chooses the cheapest valid standing sheet across them.
6. **Trace → Human review.** The runner saves its decision notes; `buyer pull` collects the arena trace and official cost breakdown. The team compares the result with the best possible cost and tests the next change offline or in the sandbox.

The runner sends one message at a time within a case and serves the supplier whose reply has waited longest. Cases run in parallel during a wave. It limits the optional model to 15 seconds, stops negotiating 90 seconds before a final wave cap, and rereads arena state after a send or close returns HTTP 409.

## What each box does

| Box | Plain-language role | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **Arena** | Supplies the case, opening quotes, supplier replies and final result. The kit handles API calls, session state and quote attachments. | `arena_kit.client`, `arena_kit.play`, [API brief](api.md) |
| **Runner** | Opens cases, chooses which supplier needs a reply, sends one message at a time within a case, watches clocks and runs final waves in parallel. | [`buyer/runner.py`](../buyer/runner.py), [`buyer/cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) |
| **Data package** | Read-only supplier records, citable facts and documents. The Sunday release joins ID lookup; the package's SQL database stays separate. | `arena_kit.data.DataPackage`, [`buyer/claims.py`](../buyer/claims.py), [`buyer/personas.py`](../buyer/personas.py) |
| **Negotiator** | Owns one case's policy: sets up suppliers, reads replies, plans offers, selects claims and chooses the close action. | `Negotiator` in [`buyer/policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) |
| **Side** | Remembers one supplier's quote, standard terms, profile, planned terms, offers, counters, asks and pending message. | `Side` in [`buyer/policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) |
| **Cost engine** | Uses the kit's published cost function, estimates supplier value, searches allowed term combinations and rejects unacceptable deals. | [`buyer/economics.py`](../buyer/economics.py), `arena_kit.cost` |
| **Optional model** | Writes one middle paragraph in the email. It does not choose prices, terms, claims or accept actions. | [`buyer/llm.py`](../buyer/llm.py) |
| **Writer** | Assembles the code-chosen proposal, figures and cited claims into an email; prepares the model brief and template fallback. | [`buyer/writer.py`](../buyer/writer.py), `Negotiator.send` |
| **Close gate** | Finds the cheapest acceptable *standing* supplier sheet or walks away. It checks must-haves and estimated cost against the alternative. | `Negotiator.best_offer`, `Negotiator.close`, `economics.deal_cost` |
| **Trace and back office** | Hold the arena's full conversation, result and official cost breakdown after a session. | `buyer pull` in [`buyer/cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) |
| **Human review** | Compares decisions with the result, records a finding, changes code and tests again. This is outside the live agent. | [`learnings.md`](learnings.md), [`analysis/explore.py`](../analysis/explore.py) |

### What is binding

The kit's `complete_offer` fills normal planned sheets to the case's negotiable fields. When mirroring a supplier alternative, `economics.quoted_offer` preserves its exact effective package instead of snapping its values. At close, `economics.deal_cost` requires a price, `must_haves_ok` and cost below the buyer's alternative. Its cost uses `arena_kit.total_cost` with this buyer's supplier estimate, so an unknown full cost can make the relationship charge uncertain.

Only the first supplier sheet in its latest reply is a standing sheet that can be accepted. A better alternative sheet must first be sent back so the supplier makes it standing. The model's paragraph is nonbinding, but its wording still matters; [system review](system-review.md) covers the missing central outbound check.

## Every Python file in `buyer/`

| File | Responsibility and main interfaces |
|---|---|
| [`__init__.py`](../buyer/__init__.py) | Marks `buyer` as the package. It contains only a package docstring and makes no decisions. |
| [`cli.py`](../buyer/cli.py) | Command entry point. `main` parses `play`, `run` and `pull`; `load_package` builds the shared ID index; `pull` saves completed sessions, traces and back office. It also selects the kit's naive baseline when requested. |
| [`runner.py`](../buyer/runner.py) | Live orchestration. `play_case` schedules supplier turns and sends messages; `writer_budget` protects clocks; `close` retries a refused close; `play_all` runs practice cases; `play_waves` polls and runs final waves; `save` writes run notes. |
| [`policy.py`](../buyer/policy.py) | The negotiation state machine. `Side` stores one supplier's state; `Negotiator.setup` builds its plan, `move` responds to a reply, `next_price` paces concessions, `pick` chooses claims, `send` assembles a move, `commit` and `rollback` track delivery, and `best_offer` and `close` choose the final action. `asks` reads fixed-form email requests. |
| [`economics.py`](../buyer/economics.py) | All cost and term math. `cost` wraps the kit's total cost; `estimate` models supplier economics; `plan_terms` scores allowed packages; `value` and `price_for_value` compare packages at equal supplier value; `quoted_offer` validates an exact supplier package; `relationship_optimum` handles cases where a lower price raises relationship cost; `deal_cost` is the accept gate. |
| [`claims.py`](../buyer/claims.py) | The citable argument bank. `ClaimBank` looks up facts and IDs, builds sentences about should-cost, orders, indexes, forecasts, notice, supplier notes, scorecards and rival quotes, then ranks them through `for_supplier`. `rival_offer` cites another bidder's current standing sheet. |
| [`personas.py`](../buyer/personas.py) | Supplier reading. `supplier_texts` gathers notes, letters, news and quote remarks; `signals_in` detects traits such as cash need or full capacity; `profile` derives owner, country, signals, cost of money and email tone. Unknown suppliers get a neutral profile. |
| [`writer.py`](../buyer/writer.py) | Email composition. `describe` names the code-chosen terms; `statements` writes binding volume or fixed-payment answers; `facts` and `brief` constrain what the model may say; `email` combines paragraph, claims and proposal; `keepalive_message` handles a waiting bidder. |
| [`llm.py`](../buyer/llm.py) | Optional model connection. `complete_from_env` builds the chat-completions caller; `paragraph` enforces a 15 second wall-clock ceiling and drops output with digits, IDs or leak phrases. The template works when no model is configured or the call fails. |

The buyer wraps `arena_kit`; it does not patch it. [`design.md`](design.md) separates planned agent components from this implemented path. [`system-review.md`](system-review.md) records the failure paths and improvement order. [A more agentic buyer](agentic-approach.md) proposes one bounded next step.

"""The research team, before the first e-mail: four specialist subagents each study one group of
the data about a supplier (the groups of `docs/design.md`, "What feeds the brief"), a lead
researcher consolidates their findings and past lessons into a negotiating strategy, and a
supplier and a buyer subagent rehearse the arguments against each other (`rehearsal.py`).

The strategy is about what to put on the table, not how fast to move: the terms this supplier is
likely to value more than they cost us, which arguments it will accept, the tone. Code collects
every figure a subagent sees and checks everything it returns: a proposed trade is priced with
the cost function and offered only at a price that costs us no more than our main proposal. No
brief (no model, a timeout): the plain engine."""

import json
import logging
import time

from . import llm, memory, rehearsal

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
BUDGET_S = 40.0  # the whole team per case, before the session opens (no supplier clock runs yet)
STAGE_S = 13.0  # the specialists; then the lead and the demo supplier; then the demo buyer
TRADES = 2  # terms the lead may put next to our main proposal
NOISE = ("holiday", "iso ", "certificate", "contact person", "packaging", "trade fair")
CLAIM_KINDS = ("should_cost", "order_history", "index", "notice", "rival", "forecast", "scorecard", "hedged")
CACHE = {}  # case_id -> briefs: a case resumed after a crash must not wait for the team again

# group -> (the data it studies, what it should find out)
GROUPS = {
    "economics": (
        "the case file, our should-cost estimate, the supplier's price history and the indices of its cost drivers",
        "how far its price sits above its cost, whether its cost drivers justify its price, "
        "and how much room there is on price",
    ),
    "persona": (
        "its company profile, its letters, our call and meeting notes, news about it and how we pay it",
        "who decides there and what moves them: cash, capacity, the relationship, approvals, frozen prices",
    ),
    "history": (
        "our past negotiations with it, our contract and its clauses, and how the part is sourced",
        "how far it usually moves from what it asks, what the contract obliges it to, and how dependent "
        "each side is on the other",
    ),
    "leverage": (
        "its delivery and quality record, our forecast, our order prices and rival quotes for the part",
        "which verified facts argue for a lower price or better terms, and which would argue its case",
    ),
}
SPECIALIST = """You are the {name} analyst in the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump
maker. Before we negotiate with a supplier you study one group of our data: {scope}.
From the data below report {goal}.
Use only the data given. When it says nothing useful, return no findings.
Return JSON only: {{"findings": [up to 4 short sentences, the most important first],
"leverage": "ours" | "balanced" | "theirs"}}"""

ARENA = """What we know about how these suppliers negotiate:
- Their first counter is a cap plus the verified arguments they accept, not a reaction to how low we
  open. Opening far below the quote buys nothing and costs patience.
- After that they concede a shrinking step per round, only after a move from us, and stop after a
  few counters with a final offer. They agree the moment our price reaches the counter they would make.
- Typical: a foundry or family firm with rising wages drops about 3 % first and then small steps
  over up to 5 counters; a raw-material distributor drops 8 to 10 % first and then almost nothing;
  a small job shop with free machines drops 10 to 18 % and keeps moving; a supplier with frozen
  list prices barely moves on price; a fully booked one or one selling near its cost ends after 1
  or 2 counters.
- Patience ends at a cumulative gap of about 0.4 between our prices and theirs, 0.15 to 0.2 for a
  touchy supplier."""

LEAD = (
    """You are the lead researcher of the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Your analysts
studied one supplier before a negotiation. Consolidate their findings into a negotiating strategy.
Our price engine sets the prices and the pace; your job is what we put on the table and how we
argue.

"""
    + ARENA
    + """

Return JSON only:
{"trades": up to 2 objects {"field": a negotiable field of the case other than unit_price,
  "value": one of that field's allowed options exactly as the case lists it, "why": one short
  sentence}. A trade is a term this supplier is likely to value more than it costs us: faster
  payment for one short of cash, a later delivery or a longer contract for a full order book, an
  index clause for one exposed to a volatile material, more volume for idle machines. Code prices
  each trade and offers it next to our main proposal at a price that costs us no more, so the
  supplier's choice shows what it values. [] when the findings point to none.
 "claim_order": the kinds of argument this supplier will accept, strongest first, from: KINDS.
 "tone": "warm" or "businesslike".
 "notes": two or three sentences for the colleague who writes our e-mails: who this supplier is,
  what it cares about and what we can honestly offer it. No figures, no dates.
 "reason": one sentence on why this strategy.}"""
).replace("KINDS", ", ".join(CLAIM_KINDS))


def digest(pkg, case, sid, group):
    """The data one specialist studies, as text; empty when the package knows nothing here."""
    parts = case.get("parts") or []
    part = parts[0] if parts else None
    keys = {"part": (part,), "sid": (sid,), "part_sid": (part, sid), "doc": (case.get("trigger_doc"),)}
    out = [block(title, rows(pkg, sql, keys[key], limit)) for title, sql, key, limit in TABLES[group]]
    if group == "economics":
        out.append(block("COST DRIVERS OF THE PART (weight, index change over 12 months in %)", index_moves(pkg, part)))
    if group == "persona":
        out.append(block("LETTERS AND NOTES", letters(pkg, sid)))
    return "\n".join(filter(None, out))


def clamp(raw, case):
    """The lead's strategy with every value from the case or from its list; junk is dropped."""
    options = case.get("term_options") or {}
    trades = []
    for t in raw.get("trades") if isinstance(raw.get("trades"), list) else []:
        field = t.get("field") if isinstance(t, dict) else None
        if field in case.get("negotiable", []) and field != "unit_price" and t.get("value") in options.get(field, []):
            trades.append({"field": field, "value": t["value"], "why": " ".join(str(t.get("why") or "").split())[:160]})
    order = raw.get("claim_order")
    return {
        "trades": trades[:TRADES],
        "claim_order": [k for k in order if k in CLAIM_KINDS] if isinstance(order, list) else [],
        "tone": raw.get("tone") if raw.get("tone") in ("warm", "businesslike") else None,
        "notes": " ".join(str(raw.get("notes") or "").split())[:600],
        "reason": str(raw.get("reason") or "")[:300],
    }


def briefs(case, pkg, complete, budget_s=BUDGET_S):
    """{supplier_id: brief} for a case: the specialists' findings, the lead's checked strategy and
    the demo bidding's playbook. {} without a model; a supplier whose lead was late has no brief."""
    if complete is None:
        return {}
    if case["case_id"] in CACHE:
        return CACHE[case["case_id"]]
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    end = t0 + budget_s
    head = case_brief(case)
    suppliers = case.get("suppliers") or []
    known = pkg is not None and any(pkg.lookup(r) for r in case.get("refs") or [])
    jobs = {}
    for sid in suppliers:
        for group, (scope, goal) in GROUPS.items():
            data = digest(pkg, case, sid, group) if known else ""
            if data:
                system = SPECIALIST.format(name=group, scope=scope, goal=goal)
                jobs[sid, group] = llm.submit(complete, system, f"{head}\n\nSUPPLIER {sid}\n{data}")
    stage = min(end, time.monotonic() + STAGE_S)
    found = {key: llm.read_json(f, stage - time.monotonic()) for key, f in jobs.items()}
    lessons = memory.recall(case)
    second = {}
    for sid in suppliers:
        findings = {g: (found.get((sid, g)) or {}) for g in GROUPS}
        report = "\n".join(
            f"{g.upper()} (leverage: {f.get('leverage', 'unknown')}): "
            + " ".join(str(x) for x in f.get("findings") or [])
            for g, f in findings.items()
            if f.get("findings")
        )
        user = "\n\n".join(
            filter(
                None,
                [
                    head,
                    f"SUPPLIER {sid}, one of {len(suppliers)} in this case",
                    block("ANALYSTS", [report or "No data on this supplier: judge from the case alone."]),
                    block("LESSONS FROM EARLIER NEGOTIATIONS OF THIS KIND", lessons),
                ],
            )
        )
        second[sid] = (findings, user, llm.submit(complete, LEAD, user), llm.submit(complete, rehearsal.SUPPLIER, user))
    stage = min(end, time.monotonic() + STAGE_S)
    third = {}
    for sid, (findings, user, lead, supplier) in second.items():
        strategy = llm.read_json(lead, stage - time.monotonic())
        view = rehearsal.supplier_view(llm.read_json(supplier, stage - time.monotonic()))
        buyer = None
        if view["arguments"]:  # the demo bidding's second half: our side answers its arguments
            buyer = llm.submit(complete, rehearsal.BUYER, f"{user}\n\n{rehearsal.exchange(view)}")
        third[sid] = (findings, strategy, view, buyer)
    stage = min(end, time.monotonic() + STAGE_S)
    out = {}
    for sid, (findings, strategy, view, buyer) in third.items():
        if strategy is None:
            continue
        out[sid] = {
            **clamp(strategy, case),
            "playbook": rehearsal.playbook(
                view, llm.read_json(buyer, stage - time.monotonic()), any(findings.values())
            ),
            "findings": {g: f.get("findings") for g, f in findings.items() if f.get("findings")},
        }
    log.info("%s research in %.1fs: %s", case["case_id"], time.monotonic() - t0, json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))
    CACHE[case["case_id"]] = out
    return out
"""The demo bidding before the real one: a supplier subagent and a buyer subagent argue the case
against each other. The supplier, in character and knowing what our analysts found, says which
arguments it will bring, which weak points it hopes we miss and what it would give price for. The
buyer answers each argument and picks the weak points to press. What comes out is a playbook for
the real bidding: the live analyst matches a supplier e-mail to one of the expected arguments and
the writer gets our prepared answer. Words only: every price and term stays with code, and a line
with a figure in it is dropped (the writer may not use one)."""

import re

SUPPLIER = """You play the sales lead of a supplier in a rehearsal of a negotiation with your customer
Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Below is the case and what the customer's analysts found out about your
company. Stay in character and be honest with yourself: this rehearsal is private.
Return JSON only:
{"arguments": the up to 4 arguments you will bring to defend your price or refuse a request, one
  sentence each, strongest first,
 "weak_points": the up to 3 points in your position you hope the customer does not raise, one
  sentence each,
 "wants": the up to 3 things other than price you would give a better price for, one short phrase each}
Write no figures, dates or names."""

BUYER = """You are the senior buyer of Hollerau Pumpenwerke in a rehearsal of a negotiation. Below is
the case, what our analysts found, and what the supplier's sales lead said in the rehearsal: the
arguments it will bring and the weak points it hopes we miss.
Find our best answer to each of its arguments: reasoning that is fair, factual and hard to
dismiss. An answer may acknowledge its point, put it in proportion and point to what we already
bring (our full volume, a long term, reliable payment). An answer never promises or offers
anything new, sets no condition, and is never a threat, a deadline, a bluff or a request for its
cost breakdown (all tested, none works).
Return JSON only:
{"rebuttals": one object per supplier argument, {"to": the argument's number, "answer": our answer
  in one or two sentences},
 "press": the up to 2 weak points worth raising, each as one polite, respectful sentence we could
  write, taken only from what the analysts found, never about its finances; [] when the analysts
  found nothing}
Write no figures, dates or names: code adds the data."""

DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")


def exchange(view):
    """The supplier's side of the rehearsal as the buyer subagent reads it."""
    numbered = "\n".join(f"{i}. {a}" for i, a in enumerate(view["arguments"], 1))
    weak = "\n".join(f"- {w}" for w in view["weak_points"])
    return f"THE SUPPLIER'S ARGUMENTS:\n{numbered}\nWEAK POINTS IT HOPES WE MISS:\n{weak or '- none named'}"


def playbook(view, raw, informed=True):
    """The rehearsal's result: each expected argument with our answer ("" when the buyer found
    none), the weak points to press and what the supplier wants besides price. `informed`: our
    analysts had data on this supplier; without it a "weak point" is a guess, and we never write
    a supplier something our records do not show."""
    raw = raw or {}
    answers = {}
    for r in raw.get("rebuttals") if isinstance(raw.get("rebuttals"), list) else []:
        if isinstance(r, dict) and isinstance(r.get("to"), int) and lines([r.get("answer")], 1, 400):
            answers[r["to"]] = lines([r["answer"]], 1, 400)[0]
    return {
        "arguments": view["arguments"],
        "rebuttals": [answers.get(i, "") for i in range(1, len(view["arguments"]) + 1)],
        "press": lines(raw.get("press"), 2) if informed else [],
        "wants": view["wants"],
    }
"""The live analyst: reads each supplier e-mail as it arrives (the opening quote included) and
tells the bidder the mood of the person writing and the tactic for our next move, so the bidding
follows the supplier we actually meet and not only the one in our files. It also matches the
e-mail to the arguments the demo bidding expected, so the writer gets our prepared answer.
Everything it returns comes from a fixed list; the policy decides what each value changes. Traits
that move anchors or rates stay with the patterns in `personas.py`: a model's guess there costs too
much."""

from . import llm

TIMEOUT_S = 6.0
MOODS = ("warm", "neutral", "irritated", "pressured")
TACTICS = ("steady", "hold", "close_in", "argue")
ASKS = ("volume", "proof", "payment", "target")  # the kinds `policy.asks` reads

SYSTEM = """You are the analyst next to our buyer at Hollerau Pumpenwerke during a negotiation. Read
the supplier's latest e-mail and say who we are dealing with right now and what to do next.
Return JSON only:
{"mood": the mood of the person writing: "warm", "neutral", "irritated" or "pressured",
 "tactic": our best next move, one of:
   "hold" - it still concedes or signals room to move: we move less than usual,
   "close_in" - it says in so many words that this is nearly its last step or that its patience
     is used up: we move further towards its price to keep the talks alive,
   "argue" - it brings an argument we can answer or doubts our data: we answer it with evidence,
   "steady" - none of these,
 "argument": the number of the EXPECTED ARGUMENT its e-mail makes, or 0 if none,
 "asks": what it asks of us, from this list only: volume, proof, payment, target,
 "notes": one or two sentences for the colleague who writes our reply: what this person cares
  about right now and how to answer them. No figures, no dates.}"""


def read(complete, case, body, ours, theirs, arguments=(), timeout=TIMEOUT_S):
    """{mood, tactic, argument, asks, notes} for a supplier e-mail, every value from its list; None
    when the model is off, late or wrong. `ours`, `theirs`: the price paths so far; `arguments`:
    what the demo bidding expected this supplier to say (`argument` indexes them from 1)."""
    expected = "\n".join(f"{i}. {a}" for i, a in enumerate(arguments, 1)) or "none prepared"
    user = (
        f"CASE: {case.get('title')} ({case.get('type')}, goal {case['buyer'].get('category_goal')})\n"
        f"OUR PRICES SO FAR: {ours}\nITS PRICES SO FAR: {theirs}\nEXPECTED ARGUMENTS:\n{expected}\n"
        f"ITS E-MAIL:\n{(body or '')[:2500]}"
    )
    raw = llm.ask_json(complete, SYSTEM, user, min(timeout, TIMEOUT_S))
    if raw is None:
        return None
    asks = raw.get("asks")
    argument = raw.get("argument")
    return {
        "mood": raw.get("mood") if raw.get("mood") in MOODS else "neutral",
        "tactic": raw.get("tactic") if raw.get("tactic") in TACTICS else "steady",
        "argument": argument if isinstance(argument, int) and 0 < argument <= len(arguments) else 0,
        "asks": [a for a in asks if a in ASKS] if isinstance(asks, list) else [],
        "notes": " ".join(str(raw.get("notes") or "").split())[:400],
    }
"""What the team learned, case after case: after a case closes, a debrief subagent reads how it
went and writes one lesson; the lead researcher reads the lessons of similar cases before the
next one. Lessons are keyed on features (goal, case type, owner type, traits), never on a case or
supplier ID, and code writes every figure in them."""

import json
import logging
import threading
from pathlib import Path

from . import llm

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
LESSONS = Path(__file__).parent / "lessons.jsonl"  # committed: the final machine starts with them
RECALL = 5
LOCK = threading.Lock()

DEBRIEF = """You are the debrief analyst of the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Below is how
one negotiation went, in shares of the supplier's quote: where we opened, our price path, its
price path, its reasons in its own words, and the score (1.0 is the best deal that was possible,
0 is no better than its first offer).
Our team can change four things only: which terms it offers as a trade next to its main proposal,
which kind of argument it cites first, how it answers the supplier's arguments, and its tone.
Code sets the prices and the pace. Threats, deadlines, bluffs and requests for cost data have been tested and
do not work, never suggest them.
Write the one lesson for the next negotiation with this KIND of supplier (owner type, traits,
goal): what its path and reasons show about how it concedes and when it stops, and which of the
four things to do differently, or to keep if the score is high.
Never name the supplier, the part, the case or any ID, and give no absolute prices.
Return JSON only: {"lesson": "one or two short sentences"}"""


def reasons(result, sid):
    """Its reasons round by round, from the replay (practice and sandbox)."""
    out = []
    for step in result.get("trace") or []:
        if step.get("actor") == sid and step.get("reasons"):
            out.append(f"round {step.get('round')}: " + " ".join(str(r) for r in step["reasons"])[:400])
    return out


def record(case, neg, result, complete):
    """Append this case's lesson. Only a case with a score teaches (the final shows none)."""
    if result.get("score") is None:
        return None
    sides = [s for s in neg.sides.values() if s.ours]
    if not sides:
        return None
    won = neg.sides.get(result.get("supplier_id"))
    row = {
        **features(case, sides),
        "deal": bool(result.get("deal")),
        "score": round(result["score"], 3),
        "threads": [path(s) for s in ([won] if won and won.ours else sides)],
    }
    user = json.dumps({**row, "reasons": [r for s in sides for r in reasons(result, s.sid)][-12:]}, ensure_ascii=False)
    answer = llm.ask_json(complete, DEBRIEF, user) or {}
    row["lesson"] = " ".join(str(answer.get("lesson") or "").split())[:300]
    with LOCK, LESSONS.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return row


def recall(case, n=RECALL):
    """The latest lessons of the most similar cases (same goal, then same case type), as lines."""
    if not LESSONS.is_file():
        return []
    rows = []
    for line in LESSONS.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        try:
            rows.append(json.loads(line))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    goal, kind = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), case.get("type")
    ranked = sorted(enumerate(rows), key=lambda r: ((r[1].get("goal") == goal) + (r[1].get("type") == kind), r[0]))
    out = []
    for _, r in ranked[-n:]:
        if r.get("goal") != goal and r.get("type") != kind:
            continue
        t = (r.get("threads") or [{}])[0]
        out.append(
            f"{r.get('goal')} {r.get('type')}, {r.get('bidders')} bidder(s), owner {'/'.join(r.get('owners') or [])}, "
            f"traits {r.get('signals')}: opened at {t.get('opened')} of the quote, offered trades "
            f"{t.get('trades') or []}, its prices {t.get('theirs')}, score {r.get('score')}. {r.get('lesson') or ''}"
        )
    return out

The diagram above shows the eight model subagents in three phases, with code sitting between them and every binding number.

- **Before the session** ([research.py](buyer/research.py), [rehearsal.py](buyer/rehearsal.py)): the four specialists run in parallel per supplier, each on one group of data. Their findings go to both the lead researcher and the demo supplier, which run in parallel. The demo buyer then answers the demo supplier's arguments. Each stage gets about 13 s of the 40 s budget.
- **The brief**: `clamp()` keeps only trades whose field and value the case allows, and `playbook()` drops any line containing a digit. A supplier whose lead answered late gets no brief, and the plain price engine plays.
- **During the session** ([analyst.py](buyer/analyst.py), [policy.py](buyer/policy.py)): the live analyst reads each supplier e-mail within 6 s and returns values from fixed lists only. `Negotiator` decides what those values change, and the writer's paragraph cannot alter the sheet.
- **After the case** ([memory.py](buyer/memory.py)): the debrief analyst writes one lesson, only when the result carries a score, so the final adds none. `recall()` hands the five most similar lessons (same goal or case type) to the next research run.

The diagram simplifies two things:

- The brief is drawn as one arrow into `Negotiator`, but its parts are used in different places: trades and claim order by the policy, the playbook by the live analyst, and the notes by the writer.
- The recalled lessons reach the lead, the demo supplier and the demo buyer, since all three share the same prompt body.

The boxes are clickable if you want to drill into one.

# Learnings

## Louis subagent-team practice batch (2026-10-11)

One hosted Practice session was run for each available case. All ten reached a deal; the mean
score was 0.7772. The dashboard reference at the time was 0.802, but this single batch is not a
paired comparison and does not establish a reliable gain or regression.

| Case | Score |
|---|---:|
| P01 | 0.9085 |
| P02 | 0.7347 |
| P03 | 0.9276 |
| P04 | 0.8604 |
| P05 | 0.8218 |
| P07 | 0.7313 |
| P08 | 0.7036 |
| P10 | 0.6785 |
| P11 | 0.7099 |
| P18 | 0.6957 |

The run recorded 127 subagent attempts, 121 successes and 6 timeouts; the writer had 37 attempts,
29 successes, 7 rejected paragraphs, 2 deadline skips and 1 timeout. Fallbacks kept sessions
running. These counts describe model reliability, not its effect on scores. The batch used the
`louis/subagent-team` base with the candidate safeguards; it is diagnostic evidence only.

Observations from the arena and the data package, with evidence. An entry says what happened and
how often, not what to do; what the agent does is in `design.md`. Most entries rest on one to
three sessions with one supplier. The sandbox bots are deterministic per sheet path; the practice
suppliers vary 1 to 2 % between runs with the same sheets. Sessions: `exports/` (schema in
`exports/README.md`), `logs/sessions/`, `logs/runs/`. Tags: `arena` seen in a session, `data` from
the package, `rules` from `docs/api.md` or the kit.

## Where we stand (Saturday night)

Mean of best scores 0.776, rank 3 of 24 on the practice board (first 0.838); the last ten-case
validation run of one code version averaged 0.727. Record = best of all teams on `/v1/live`,
house agent in brackets; records average 0.84.

| Case | Goal | Ours | Deal | Record (house) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | stabilise | 0.974 | 130.18, Nov, 14 d | 0.995 (0.966) |
| P02 | stabilise | 0.735 | 361.67, 90 d, CU clause 5 % deadband | 0.847 (0.740) |
| P03 | stabilise | 0.923 | 432.15, 90 d, 24 m | 0.936 (0.925) |
| P04 | routine | 0.860 | 4.94, 90 d, 36 m | 0.874 (0.860) |
| P05 | leverage RFQ | 0.828 | Dralveck 27.86, 14 d, 35 d | 0.824 (0.555) |
| P07 | routine | 0.751 | 5.35, 45 d, 36 m | 0.779 (0.782) |
| P08 | leverage | 0.670 | 5.26, AS-14404 clause | 0.916 (0.752) |
| P10 | secure_supply | 0.679 | 31.50, 56 d, 36 m | 0.702 (0.686) |
| P11 | quality_first | 0.710 | 45.50, 300 ppm | 0.807 (0.314) |
| P18 | leverage | 0.688 | 5.00, AS-14404 clause | 0.677 (0.386) |

Records decode to about P08 5.21 to 5.35 depending on the clause, P02 369.5, P11 44.9. How those
teams got there is unknown. C_best decodes to P08 5.10 fixed (4.94 with a 0 % clause), P18 4.73,
P02 368.34 at 90 days, P11 43.91 with chargeback 500, P10 28.21 at 42 days, P07 5.03, P04 4.93
against a frozen 4.94.

## Cost (`rules`)

- The category goal sets the rates: fallback risk leverage 3 %, routine 5 %, quality_first 8 %,
  stabilise 10 %, secure_supply 25 %; a relationship charge only in stabilise (sustainable margin
  0.5 to 8 %) and secure_supply (4 to 10 %). The charge grows with the square of the first 5
  missing margin points, so C has a minimum below the sustainable margin (D01: 2 points below its
  4 %). It also moves with payment terms (P02: 5,483 at 368.70 and 90 days, 901 at 366.41 and
  14 days).
- Uncovered need costs `fallback_unit_price` plus the risk rate; coverage is

| Property | Evidence | Why it matters |

**The most leverage is in removing low-score outcomes on unfamiliar structure, not in better prices.** You have until 12:00 (it was 07:09 when I checked), and the price path is where further tuning would overfit.

This is based on all 310 pulled practice sessions in `logs/sessions/practice/`, which span every code version and branch. I have not checked which of the failures below current `main` already guards.

## What the sessions show

- **Within-case spread is far larger than the gap to the records.** Best-per-case averages 0.776 against records of 0.84 (`docs/learnings.md`), a gap of 0.06. The same case swings by 0.6 to 0.7 between sessions:

| Case | Worst deal | Best deal | What the worst one got wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| P08 | 0.108 | 0.737 | 12 months instead of 36; uncovered need cost 3.1x the whole scoring span |
| P18 | 0.059 | 0.756 | Same: 12 months, uncovered need 2.0x the span |
| P02 | 0.0 | 0.735 | Price pushed to 349.05, relationship charge 3.0x the span; or copper clause without a deadband, 0.85x the span |

- **The disasters are term-structure errors, not price errors.** 16 of 310 sessions scored below 0.3, and 12 of those were accepted deals. Every one I inspected was a sheet whose non-price terms cost more than the price saved.
- **The price path is saturated.** Your own log says first counters do not react to anchor or claims, a 40 % move gets the same as 30 %, and the last mean gain above 0.01 came with v10. Run-to-run noise on identical sheets (P08: 5.26 to 5.57) is larger than any remaining tuning effect.
- **The subagent team has no measured gain.** Its one batch scored 0.777 against a 0.802 reference, unpaired, with 6 of 127 subagent calls timing out.

## Where I would spend the remaining hours

1. **Run a structural invariant test over all 21 case files on the simulator.** For every sheet we send or accept, check that `total_cost` is no worse than the opening quote's and that no non-price component exceeds the price saving. It is free and uses no quota. It covers the eleven case files never played live (P06 tooling, P09, P12 to P17, P19).
2. **Trace one new supplier end to end at 08:00.** The Sunday release reaches the ID index but not SQL (R3 in `docs/system-review.md`). `research.digest`, `ClaimBank.query` and `Negotiator.full_cost` all read SQL, so a new supplier may get a neutral profile, no should-cost and no brief. Since the final includes new suppliers, this could affect every wave.
3. **Be conservative when full cost is unknown in stabilise and secure_supply cases.** Without an estimate, the close gate sees no relationship charge (R6), which is the P02 failure. A new supplier from step 2 lands exactly here.
4. **Fix R1 and R2 only if a test reproduces them.** A case that crashes twice is never resubmitted, and a fourth bidder can run out its 60 s clock; either scores about 0 on that case.
5. **Freeze the price path, and decide the team on reliability alone.** Keep the team only if a four-bidder simulator run shows it cannot delay a send.

I can write the invariant test from step 1 now; it would also tell us whether current `main` still allows the P08, P18 and P02 failures.

        )
        if full_cost:
            # also for a supplier selling at our cost estimate: below the optimum a lower price costs
            # us more than it saves, and pushing on made Nordmark withdraw (P02 v1)
            s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
        safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
        s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
        order = brief.get("claim_order") or []  # the arguments the lead expects this supplier to accept, first
        s.claims.sort(key=lambda c: order.index(c["kind"]) if c["kind"] in order else len(order))
        self.note(
            sid,
            "setup",
            quote=quote,
            std=s.std,
            profile=s.prof,
            full_cost=full_cost,
            near_cost=near_cost,
            terms=s.terms,
            quote_at_terms=s.quote,
            anchor=s.anchor,
            target=s.target,
            budget=s.budget,
            claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
        )
        return s

    def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
        `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
        s, events = self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
        self.writer_s = writer_s
        s.prev_state = s.state
        last = latest(events)
        status = last.get("status")
        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
            s.state = "ended"
            return None
        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
        if not sheets:
            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
            return None
        std_before = s.std
        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
        if fresh:
            terms_before = dict(s.terms)
            estimate_before = dict(s.est)
            self.adopt(s, sheets)
            s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
            s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
            s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
            s.last_reply = last
            s.asks = asks(last.get("body"))
            self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
            if self.briefs is not None and status not in DONE:
                self.listen(s, last.get("body"))
            economics_changed = s.terms != terms_before or s.est != estimate_before or s.std != std_before
            if s.target is not None and economics_changed:
                s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
                    self.case,
                    s.terms,
                    s.std,
                    s.est,
                    s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85,
                    max(s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85, s.quote, s.target, s.theirs[-1]),
                )
        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
        if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
            s.state = "done"
            return None
        left = self.moves_left(s, events)
        if status in DONE or left <= 0:
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        if s.ours and s.target and theirs <= s.target:
            # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
            s.state = "closing"
            sheet = eco.at_price(s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))
            if self.same_offer(s.last_sent_terms, sheet):
                s.state = "done"
                self.note(sid, "no_progress", reason="relationship target already offered")
                return None
            return self.send(s, [sheet], [], events, theirs)
        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
        sheets = [eco.at_price(s.terms, price)]
        if not s.ours and s.trades:
            sheets += safe(lambda: self.trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
        elif s.ours:
            sheets += safe(lambda: self.need_trade_sheets(s, sheets[0]), [])[:2]
        switched_trade_keys = set()
        if self.same_offer(s.last_sent_terms, sheets[0]):
            if len(sheets) == 1:
                s.state = "done"
                self.note(sid, "no_progress", reason="unchanged price and terms")
                return None
            # Do not resend the old primary sheet. Move the thread onto the best new package,
            # whose buyer cost is lower and whose estimated supplier value matches the main offer.
            switched_trade_keys = self.trade_keys(sheets)
            sheet = sheets[1]
            old_target = s.target
            self.switch(s, sheet, "cost-checked response to a supplier need")
            if old_target is not None and s.est.get("full_cost"):
                floor = s.est["full_cost"] * 0.85
                s.target = eco.relationship_optimum(
                    self.case,
                    s.terms,
                    s.std,
                    s.est,
                    floor,
                    max(floor, s.quote, old_target, s.theirs[-1]),
                )
            sheets = [sheet]
        result = self.send(s, sheets, claims, events, theirs)
        if s.pending and switched_trade_keys:
            s.pending["trade_keys"].update(switched_trade_keys)
        return result

    def moves_left(self, s, events):
        """Messages we may still send: the arena counts a late message as a round too."""
        return moves_left(self.case, events) - s.late

    def next_price(self, s, theirs):
        """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
        large concession, and within the patience budget."""
        if not s.ours:
            return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS
        last = s.ours[-1]
        conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
        fraction = FRACTION * (HOLD if s.tactic == "hold" else 1.0)
        price = step(last, theirs, conceded, len(s.ours) == 1, fraction, s.budget, sum(s.gaps), s.term_change)
        if s.tactic == "close_in":
            price = min(max(price, last + CLOSE_IN * (theirs - last)), theirs * 0.998)
        return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS + (s.tactic == "argue")  # an argument gets evidence

    def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):
        """Its final word, its agreement or our last message: if one of its alternatives costs us
        less than its standing sheet, send that sheet back so it agrees to it; else done."""
        case = self.case
        std = s.std
        c_stand = eco.deal_cost(case, sheets[0]["terms"], std, s.est)
        alts = []
        for sh in sheets[1:]:
            terms = eco.quoted_offer(case, sh["terms"], std)
            c = eco.deal_cost(case, terms, std, s.est) if terms is not None else None
            if c is not None:
                alts.append((c, terms))
        if alts and left > 0:
            c, terms = min(alts, key=lambda row: row[0])
            if c_stand is None or c < c_stand - 1.0:
                s.state = "mirror"
                return self.send(s, [terms], [], events, theirs)
        s.state = "done"
        return None

    def best_offer(self, threads):
        """(C, supplier, term_sheet_id) of the cheapest acceptable standing sheet (only a standing
        sheet can be accepted; alternatives were sent back to become standing). One supplier's
        broken data skips that supplier, never the close."""
        best = None
        for sid, events in threads.items():
            if latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
                continue
            oid, terms = standing(events)
            c = safe(functools.partial(self.deal_cost, sid, events, terms)) if oid else None
            if c is not None and (best is None or c < best[0]):
                best = (c, sid, oid)
        return best

    def deal_cost(self, sid, events, terms):
        side = self.sides.get(sid) or Side(sid)
        return eco.deal_cost(self.case, terms, standard_terms(events) or side.std, side.est)

    def close(self, threads):
        best = self.best_offer(threads)
        if best is None:
            live = live_threads(threads) or list(threads)
            self.note(None, "walk_away")
            return {"supplier_id": live[0], "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
        self.note(best[1], "accept", c=best[0], offer=best[2])
        return {"supplier_id": best[1], "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": best[2]}}}

    def note(self, sid, what, **kw):
        entry = {"t": round(time.time(), 1), "supplier": sid, "what": what, **kw}
        self.notes.append(entry)
        log.info(
            "%s %s %s",
            self.case["case_id"],
            sid,
            {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k not in ("claims", "std", "profile")},
        )


def step(last, theirs, conceded, first, fraction, budget, used, term_change=False):
    """Our next price after `last` against its counter `theirs`: we close `fraction` of the gap,
    hold low after a large first concession, and stay within the patience budget (`used` of it is
    spent). The real bidding and the demo bidding (`rehearsal.py`) both step with this."""
    gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
    share = fraction
    if first and conceded >= DEEP and not term_change:
        # a deep floor: a pure price drop this large means it moves fast on its own (job shops,
        # P05, D02) and agrees at our sheet next: hold the anchor (Dralveck agreed at a held
        # 27.86, at 28.07 after an 8 % step); a drop that came with terms it added (an index
        # clause, P08, P18) is not one
        share = 0.0
    left = max(0.0, budget - used)
    new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
    if budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
        new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
    price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
    price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
    price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
    return max(price, last)


def safe(fn, default=None):
    """`fn()`, or `default` when it raises: a hidden case may lack a field the data code expects,
    and a missing claim or profile must never cost the move."""
    try:
        return fn()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - logged, the move goes on with the default
        log.exception("skipped: %s", getattr(fn, "__name__", fn))
        return default

The first chart shows the price path the engine produces; the second shows the four checks it runs, in order, on every supplier reply. Everything is in [policy.py](buyer/policy.py), with the numbers in the first chart made up for a routine case.

## How the opening is set (`Negotiator.setup`)

The anchor is a share of the supplier's quote, chosen by category goal and then raised by what the data says about the supplier:

| Goal | Anchor | Patience budget |
|---|---|---|
| leverage | 0.78 | 1.0 |
| routine | 0.82 | 1.0 |
| secure_supply | 0.88 | 0.3 |
| quality_first | 0.88 | 1.0 |
| stabilise | 0.92 | 0.3 |

- **Price-frozen supplier:** anchor at least 0.95.
- **Full order book:** anchor at least 0.93, budget at most 0.16.
- **Selling near our cost estimate:** anchor at least 0.97, budget at most 0.14.
- **Price-increase case:** never open above today's price.
- **Floor:** never below 0.75 of the quote.

Non-price terms are planned once at the anchor price by `eco.plan_terms`, and the price then moves on those terms.

## How each step is sized (`step`)

- **Default:** close 30 % of the gap to its latest counter.
- **Deep first drop:** if its first counter fell 6 % or more on price alone, hold the anchor (subject to the 0.2 % minimum) instead of stepping.
- **Patience:** the gap we show is capped at half the remaining budget; a touchy supplier (budget under 0.2) never sees a gap above 1.5 %.
- **Bounds:** every sheet rises at least 0.2 % and stays 0.2 % under its counter, so we never jump to its price.
- **Live analyst:** "hold" shrinks the step to 70 %; "close_in" closes at least half the gap.

## What this means for the score

The engine never accepts on price mid-thread; it walks up until the supplier says final or undercuts us, then the close gate takes the cheapest valid standing sheet. So the final price is set mostly by where the supplier stops, which matches your log: first counters ignore the anchor, and a 40 % step got the same as 30 %.

The parts that can lose a lot are the ones outside the price walk: the terms planned at setup, the relationship target, and the close gate's view of cost when full cost is unknown. That is where the low-scoring P08, P18 and P02 sessions came from.
what does this mean: The disasters are term-structure errors

I meant that the very low scores came from the non-price fields of the accepted sheet (contract length, index clause, how far below the supplier's cost we pushed), not from paying a few cents too much per unit.

The score is computed on total cost C, and price is only one line of it. A sheet can carry a perfectly reasonable price and still score near zero if another field adds a large cost elsewhere in C. Three examples from the pulled practice sessions:

| Case | What the sheet said | Which cost line blew up | Score | Best run of the same case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P08 | 12 months instead of 36 | Uncovered need: the months not covered are bought at the fallback price, costing 3.1 times the whole scoring span | 0.108 | 0.737 |
| P18 | 12 months instead of 36 | Same, 2.0 times the span | 0.059 | 0.756 |
| P02 | The supplier's copper clause accepted with no deadband | Index clause plus index risk, 0.85 of the span | 0.0 | 0.735 |

The "span" is `C_open - C_best`, the denominator of the score, so a cost line of 1.0 times the span wipes out the whole case on its own.

P02 also has a second variant where the price itself was the trigger, but through a non-price line. We pushed down to 349.05, well below the supplier's full cost. In a stabilise case that incurs a relationship charge, which came to 3.0 times the span and left a score of 0.062. A higher price of 361.67 scored 0.735.

Why I called it the main lever:
- **Size:** in these runs a wrong term cost 0.6 to 0.7 of a case, whereas the gap between your best runs and the records is about 0.06 per case.
- **Generality:** checking every outgoing and accepted sheet's cost lines with `total_cost` is not tied to any case or supplier, so it carries over to hidden cases.

These sessions span all code versions and branches, and I have not checked whether current `main` can still produce these three sheets. The 12-month ones may be old runs or the kit's naive baseline.
how would you fix that, no code

I would fix it with one cost check that every sheet passes before we send it or accept it, plus two repairs where the check currently has nothing to compare against. First, though, I would replay the three bad sheets through the current close gate to see whether `main` still lets them through.

1. **Measure "term regret" on every sheet.** For each non-price field, hold everything else fixed and ask `total_cost` what the best allowed option would cost. The difference is what that one field is costing us. A 12-month contract in P08 would show a regret several times the whole price saving, without the code knowing anything about P08.

2. **Act on the regret, depending on where we are.**
   - *Our own sheet:* never send one with a large regret; swap in the better option before it goes out.
   - *The supplier's counter changes a term* (adds a clause, shortens the contract): price that change before following it. Either keep our term, or ask for a price cut worth at least what the change costs us.
   - *At close with moves left:* send the better-term version back so it becomes the standing sheet. The engine already does this for the supplier's own alternatives; this extends it to ours.

3. **Give the close gate a baseline when there is no alternative.** Today the gate compares against the buyer's alternative, and six of the known cases have none, so anything passes. The opening quote's cost is always computable. A deal that costs more than the opening scores below zero, and a walk-away scores zero, so the gate should walk in that case.

4. **Never let the relationship charge be invisible.** When there is no should-cost, the gate currently sees no charge at all in stabilise and secure-supply cases. I would assume the supplier's full cost is its quote minus the case's sustainable margin. The setup code already uses that as a cap when a should-cost exists, so this only makes it the fallback. The price floor then exists for unknown suppliers too, which matters for the new ones in the final.

5. **Prove it on structures we have not played.** Run all 21 case files through the simulator, and assert that no sent or accepted sheet has a large regret or costs more than the opening. Add a few perturbed copies (a field removed, an option list reordered, an unknown supplier) so the check is not tuned to the known files.

**The cost of this:**

I replayed all 13 accepted practice sheets that scored below 0.3 through the current cost code on `main` (`41cfdbc`). The replay used a neutral supplier estimate (7 % rate, no full cost), not each session's real profile.

## Correction

The 12-month sheets on P08 (0.108) and P18 (0.059) were not a contract-length error. At their prices, the best allowed contract length would have saved only about 107 EUR on P08 and 8,400 on P18. The uncovered-need line was large because it replaced the price line, not because it added cost. Those two scored low because the price barely moved from the quote (5.93 and 6.00, against 5.18 and 4.90 in the best runs). So "the disasters are term-structure errors" was too broad: it holds for P02, not for P08 and P18.

## What is still in `main`

- **The close gate accepts all 13 sheets today.** It only checks must-haves and the buyer's alternative. Four of them (two on P02, two on P04) cost more than the opening quote according to the arena, and the gate has no check against that.
- **The relationship charge is invisible without a full-cost estimate.** On the P02 sheet at 349.05, the replay computes a cost 144,000 EUR below what the arena charged. Real P02 has a should-cost, so `main` sets a target there; a new supplier without one would not get it.
- **The supplier's zero-deadband clause passes the gate.** On P02 it cost 40,000 to 78,000 EUR more than no clause at the same price; on P18 about 8,500 to 11,000.

## What is not in `main`

- **The planner does not choose these terms itself.** Run on the same quotes, it plans no clause on P02 and 36 months on P04, P08 and P18.
- **Most of the bad sessions cannot be tied to our agent.** Ten of the 13 have no run notes in `logs/runs/`, so they may be the kit's naive baseline, a teammate's branch, or an early version. The three with notes are P02 at 351.90 (0.275) and P18 with the zero-deadband clause (0.252 and 0.282).

The planner is already sound, so I would drop the "term regret on our own sheets" step. Two fixes remain worthwhile:

1. The close gate should walk away when the sheet costs more than the opening quote, but only when the case has an alternative: without one, the only data point is the no-deal P02 run at 0, and no session shows a deal scored below 0.
2. Unknown suppliers in stabilise and secure-supply cases should get a fallback full-cost estimate, so the charge is counted.

The P18 clause sessions are the one open question: I have not traced whether current `main` would still follow the supplier onto its zero-deadband clause at 5.60 to 5.70, or whether that was fixed by the v14 clause guard.

After tracing it against `main`, I would not make the two fixes I proposed, because they do not hold up. What is left is one conditional code change and two tests.

## Why I am withdrawing the two fixes

- **Close gate walking away when a sheet costs more than the opening quote:** this gains nothing. The kit's `score` clips at 0, so a deal worse than the opening scores 0, not negative. A walk-away with an alternative is scored at the alternative's cost, which the gate already compares against.
- **Assuming full cost is the quote minus the sustainable margin for unknown suppliers:** your own data contradicts it. P10 has a 10 % sustainable margin, and its best possible deal sits about 10 % below the quote, so the supplier's real cost is far lower than that assumption. The fallback would stop us near 0.97 of the quote on a P10-like case and lose much more than it protects.

## Why the bad sessions are not evidence against `main`

The three low-scoring sessions that have our run notes were all written before the last three merges:

| Session | Score | What the notes show | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| P02 `b3daba378f139d09` | 0.275 | Target set at 361.67, then a 344.50 sheet was sent anyway | The PR #18 bug already in `docs/learnings.md`; v14 (#23) touched this path |
| P18 `0e3252bf3e052258` | 0.252 | Anchor 5.68, budget 0.18, accepted 5.70 after two sends | Old anchor and budget; current leverage anchor is 0.78 |
| P18 `ad9645958336cffd` | 0.282 | Accepted 5.60 after a single counter | Early version; current code keeps stepping |

I have not replayed these on current `main`, so "fixed" is inferred from the notes and commit dates, not confirmed.

## What I would change from `main`

1. **A regression test for the P02 case (test only).** On the simulator, assert that in a relationship case no sheet we send is priced below the relationship target. This would confirm whether v14 fixed the 344.50 failure.
2. **A cost-agreement test over the pulled sessions (test only).** For every recorded deal, compare our `economics.cost` with the arena's `c_deal`. In my replay without a full-cost estimate, our figure was 144,000 EUR below the arena's on one P02 sheet. This test shows where the close gate's view is off, with no behaviour change.
3. **`Negotiator.full_cost`, only if the 08:00 check fails.** It already falls back from SQL to the case's own `cost:` facts. If the Sunday release carries should-cost for new suppliers under that prefix, nothing needs to change. If it uses another shape, that lookup is the one line to fix, and it is the real protection against an invisible relationship charge.

The best place to harden is the boundary where model output turns into behaviour, because that is where practice-specific knowledge currently leaks in. I found five such points in the code, ranked here by how much they matter for unseen cases.

| # | Where | What is fragile | Hardening |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `research.digest` | Specialists read SQL only, so a new supplier from the Sunday release gives them nothing, yet the lead still proposes trades. | Feed specialists through the ID index, as `ClaimBank` does. In code, drop the lead's trades when no specialist returned findings. |
| 2 | `memory.recall` and the `DEBRIEF` prompt | Each lesson is a causal story written from one run, then handed to the lead as guidance. | Pass only the numeric paths and scores, or only lessons backed by three or more runs with the same features. |
| 3 | The `ARENA` block in `research.py` | It hard-codes how practice archetypes concede ("a foundry drops about 3 %"). The lead does not set pace, so this is mostly noise that biases it toward known supplier types. | Cut it down to the two sentences about what a trade is for. |
| 4 | `analyst.read` → `next_price` | The only place a model moves a number: "hold" shrinks our step, "close_in" gives away at least half the gap. A misread costs real money, and the one team batch shows no gain. | Require an `evidence` field holding an exact quote from the e-mail; code checks the quote is in the body, otherwise the tactic is "steady". |
| 5 | `Negotiator.send` | Invariants are spread over planner, trades, mirror, switch and fallback paths (R5 in the review). | One check before every send: all negotiable fields present, must-haves met, price not below the relationship target, and the sheet costs us no more than the supplier's standing sheet. |

Two examples from your own files show points 1 and 2:

- **Lessons:** two of the last three entries in `lessons.jsonl` describe a zero-deadband clause as the trade offered on leverage raw-material cases, and one of those says to keep it. The replay showed that clause costing 8,500 to 11,000 EUR on P18.
- **Missing data:** with no data the lead is told "judge from the case alone". Code already suppresses the "press" points in that situation, but not the trades.

**Smaller prompt-level items:**
- **Findings carry an ID.** Ask each specialist to attach the row or document ID to every finding and drop findings without a valid one. This matches your own principle in `AGENTS.md`.
- **Writer rejections.** 7 of 37 paragraphs were thrown away whole in the last batch. Filtering per sentence would keep most of them. I rank this last: your log shows practice suppliers gave the same price to the cent for a model-written e-mail.

**What I would do before 12:00:** points 1 to 3 only remove model input, so the worst case is the plain engine, which is your tested baseline. Point 4 is a small change with a clear fallback. For point 5 I would add the check as an assertion in the simulator tests and only log it live; a new blocking gate hours before the freeze is its own risk.

Yes, two more are worth changing, and one thing that looks like a prompt problem is really in the recall code. The other four prompts I would leave alone.

## Change

1. **Rehearsal `BUYER` prompt ([buyer/rehearsal.py:25](buyer/rehearsal.py:25)).** It tells the model an answer may "point to what we already bring (our full volume, a long term, reliable payment)". Your own data contradicts "reliable payment": the package shows us paying 13 to 19 days late with seven overdue letters, and Kalwisz wrote "we often see late payments". A rebuttal built on that goes to the writer and can be thrown back at us. "A long term" and "full volume" are also not true in every case. I would replace the list with "what the case and the analysts' findings show we bring".

2. **The lead's no-data message ([buyer/research.py](buyer/research.py), in `briefs`).** When no specialist found anything, the lead is told "No data on this supplier: judge from the case alone", while its prompt says to return no trades when the findings point to none. For a new supplier the first instruction wins and it guesses. I would change the message to say that no trades should be proposed without findings, and enforce that in code as well.

3. **Lessons: change `memory.recall`, not the `DEBRIEF` prompt.** The final returns no scores, so no new lessons are written during it; only the 48 committed ones are read. Editing `DEBRIEF` therefore has no effect on Sunday. What matters is how the old lessons are presented to the lead: today each one arrives as prose advice under the heading "LESSONS FROM EARLIER NEGOTIATIONS OF THIS KIND". I would pass the numbers only (opening, paths, score) and label them as single runs.

## Leave as they are

- **`SPECIALIST`:** generic, and already says to return nothing when the data says nothing.
- **Rehearsal `SUPPLIER`:** generic role-play with no practice knowledge in it.
- **Live analyst `SYSTEM`:** the tactic definitions are strict and supplier-neutral. The quote-as-evidence check I suggested earlier is a code safeguard, not a wording fix.
- **Writer `SYSTEM`:** generic, and its bans match the output filter.

The "threats, deadlines, bluffs and cost-breakdown requests do not work" line in `BUYER` and `DEBRIEF` is also practice-derived, but I would keep it: it is backed by three runs each and 12 of 12 refusals, and it keeps the model away from behaviour your hard rules discourage anyway.

The Sunday release is downloaded to `data/release-sunday/`, the kit picks it up (`DataPackage("data/package").release` is set), and the 62 tests pass with it in place.

## What the release contains

It is small: five documents and six news items dated 1 to 10 October, all about suppliers already in the package. There are no new suppliers, no new should-cost or price rows, and the index series stay frozen at 2026-09. Only `documents.csv` and `news.csv` are in its `data/` folder.

| Supplier | What changed | Known case |
|---|---|---|
| Nordmark (`sup:70510`) | Price list 2027 applies to everyone, board has ruled out individual reductions; open on payment terms and call-off planning | P02 |
| Mairhofer (`sup:70650`) | Bought by the Strelvo group, prices set centrally, no individual reductions; open on payment, call-offs and contract length | none of the 21 |
| Rupprecht-Kessel (`sup:70720`) | Bar steel bought forward at fixed prices until June 2027 | P16 |
| Fuchsreiter (`sup:70250`) | Short-time work from November, bank watching, asks for payment within 10 days | P05 |
| Kalwisz (`sup:70140`) | Filed for insolvency, production continues under an administrator | P11 |
| Weißacher (`sup:70350`) | Credit insurer withdrew cover, its suppliers ask for prepayment | none of the 21 |
| Konvertek (`sup:70540`) | Semiconductor supply back to normal, lead times returning to about twelve weeks | none of the 21 |
| Leitner (`sup:70610`) | New logistics centre (tagged as noise) | P07 |

## What our agent does with it

The persona reader does see every release text, but its fixed patterns miss the three letters that matter most:

- **Nordmark and Mairhofer are not read as price-frozen.** The pattern expects "price list applies to all", and both letters say "price list 2027 applies to all". Neither "individual price reductions" nor "set centrally" is covered.
- **Rupprecht-Kessel is not read as hedged.** The pattern allows only letters, spaces and commas between "bought our" and "forward", and the letter says "cold-drawn", with a hyphen.
- **Mairhofer is still treated as a family firm**, with the family cost-of-money rate, although it now belongs to a group.
- **Fuchsreiter and Weißacher already carried the cash-need signal**, so nothing changes there. Kalwisz's insolvency has no signal of its own; it also only shows as cash need.

The research specialists miss most of it too: their letters come from the SQL database, which does not contain the release. In my check only 2 of the 8 suppliers had release text in the specialists' letters.

## What I would do next

Widen the two patterns in `buyer/personas.py` so they match these letters, and let the research letters read through the ID index as the persona reader does. Both are small, text-driven changes with no supplier IDs involved. With Nordmark read as price-frozen, the P02 opening would move from 0.92 to at least 0.95 of the quote, so that one is worth a sandbox or practice check before it goes in.
